title: ACA s. 48 — Conditions for enforcement of foreign awards (New York Convention) (ACA s. 48)

content.overview: Section 48 sets out the limited grounds on which enforcement of a foreign award may be refused. They include incapacity or invalid agreement, lack of proper notice or opportunity, award beyond the submission, improper composition or procedure, award not yet binding or set aside/suspended at the seat, non-arbitrability, and conflict with the public policy of India as defined by the section.

content.study:
Section 48 — Conditions for enforcement of foreign awards

Section 48 sets out the limited grounds on which enforcement of a foreign award may be refused. They include incapacity or invalid agreement, lack of proper notice or opportunity, award beyond the submission, improper composition or procedure, award not yet binding or set aside/suspended at the seat, non-arbitrability, and conflict with the public policy of India as defined by the section.

The Part II analysis must begin with the statutory definition and the Convention framework, then identify the exact condition or enforcement ground engaged. The statutory grounds should not be expanded by general merits review.
